memory_candidates.content: When extracting a deterministic data file from a prose markdown report for a mechanical comparison/diff tool, do not assume every table row's path/identifier is spelled out in full: this repo's archived decidability-programme review elides repeated directory prefixes as `.../name.lean` once a table group's first row spells it out, which silently drops 4 of 5 related records unless the extractor tracks the last full path seen in row order. Check table semantics for elision before trusting a per-row regex to be complete.

When a baseline extracted from an archived review is meant to be diffed against a live-tree-derived category, verify the archived category is actually an exhaustive enumeration before diffing it -- a curated/selective table (headline results only) will produce a flood of false 'added' lines when compared against a live source's full enumeration. Prefer diffing only well-founded 1:1-correspondence categories (e.g. two independently complete arrays) and documenting the non-diffed category's limitation explicitly in the tool's own output rather than silently shipping noisy drift lines.
